scenarios.title: Preserve hosted media across format and refusal boundaries
plannedActions: Complete the existing discussions/assets journey assertions, including deletion of the original PNG and the synthetic subscription-lapse discussion checks; then reactivate that fixture team.
PUT the 3-byte JPEG and exact-12-byte WebP signatures with valid distinct asset IDs and parameterized Content-Type, retry each with bare Content-Type, then viewer GET and HEAD both.
Capture and validate exactly two ready asset rows plus their matching R2 keys, bytes, contentType and sha256/projectId/teamId metadata.
PUT empty bytes; PUT a three-byte truncated PNG signature; PUT JPEG bytes declared WebP; PUT JPEG at an incorrect all-zero digest; PUT the deleted valid PNG with an invalid space-containing asset ID.
PUT a valid PNG signature plus one extra byte, first as a known-length 13-byte Buffer and then as a two-chunk ReadableStream with no supplied Content-Length.
POST the deleted valid PNG to the asset route; after each of all eight refusals compare every asset row and the R2 keys/content bytes/contentType/customMetadata with the two-sentinel baseline.
After all refusals, viewer GET both original media signatures and compare exact bytes.
Owner DELETE the JPEG and verify public missing-asset response, exact surviving WebP GET, and full remaining asset/R2 state equals only its captured sentinel.

Owner DELETE WebP twice, require both responses successful, and assert empty assets table/R2 listing. Require all twelve new mutation/refusal labels and zero unexpected outbound attempts before owned process/state cleanup.
expectedOutcomes: Both distinct media signatures are created once, retry successfully, and viewer GET/HEAD return exact bytes, MIME type, length and digest headers; HEAD has no body. Exactly two ready rows retain valid supplied asset IDs, project/team/uploader, MIME and byte count, and match the two R2 contents and specified metadata.

The eight named inputs return exact status/code/message and standard JSON/no-store/nosniff headers. Every refusal leaves all asset rows and R2 keys/content bytes/contentType/customMetadata unchanged, and both sentinel media remain readable.
Removing JPEG preserves the complete WebP row and specified R2 content/metadata; removing WebP then repeating DELETE leaves no rows or objects.
